text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- A parliamentary committee report on the controversial Operation Birch Tree concludes thast the secret service investopgation collected ptoentially damaging data on MPs while investigating foreign organised crime in eastern Hunghary.

- Christian Democrat MPs on the right of the party formally notified the speaker on Tuesday of their departure from the party paliamentary group, leaving the group with less than the required 15 members.

Nepszabadsag carries the list of non-Swiss owners of "sleeping accounts" in the form of paid advertisements. The owners placed their deposits in Swiss banks before 1945 and many of them fell vistim to the Holocaust.
- Japan's Demnso Corporation plans to invest $100 million in a fuel injector plant to be built in Szekesfehervar, in western Hungary.
- Eighty-six percent of Hungarians do not plan to buy a car before 2000.

- Lajos Csepi, former CEO of the state property agency, denied responsibility for the scandal surrounding Co-Nexus Rt, which is under liquidation and has cost the state four billion forints by mismanaging assets the property agency entrusted to it in 1991.
- Industry and Trade Minister Szabolcs Fazakas said Slovakia's new seven percent customes surcharge to be introduced on Monday will damage trade relations with Hungary.
